assessment:
Two wishes now, not three. Worldly Tutor left the 99 in v1.3.0 and Asceticism took the slot, so the creature search is gone. Know which of the two you are holding before you decide what is missing.

Reach first. Enlightened Tutor takes an artifact or an enchantment — 18 of them in the 99. Sarkhan's Triumph takes a Dragon creature card and nothing else — 23 in the library, since the commander sits in the command zone and no search reaches it. Exactly one card answers to both: Steel Hellkite, an Artifact Creature — Dragon, new in this version. Enumerated from cards.json, it is the only overlap between the two sets.

What the cut took with it. The four cost reducers besides eminence are Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn, Dragonspeaker Shaman and Dragonlord's Servant. Enlightened Tutor reaches the two artifacts. Sarkhan's Triumph reaches neither body — the Shaman is a Human Barbarian Shaman, the Servant a Goblin Shaman — so the two creature reducers are now draw-them-or-nothing, and so is every mana dork: Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Delighted Halfling, Faeburrow Elder and Ignoble Hierarch are all outside both searches. You draw a reducer by turn six in 42.1% of games and 55.8% with tutors modelled, mean turn 3.26 (◆ goldfish, 10,000 seeded iterations). Read that assisted figure carefully: it was measured on this list, so it already counts two tutors rather than three.

Delivery second. Sarkhan's Triumph puts the card in your hand. Enlightened Tutor shuffles and puts the card on top, so it costs you a draw step — cast it at the end of the turn before yours and collect on your own draw. Cast it on your own turn and you have paid a full rotation for nothing. One card shortens that wait and it is new: Herald's Horn with Dragon chosen looks at the top card on your upkeep and takes a Dragon creature card into your hand. Steel Hellkite is a Dragon creature card as well as an artifact, so it is the one Enlightened Tutor target the Horn can pull. For the other 17 the wait is real.

Colour third. Enlightened Tutor asks {W}: 81.0% on curve from lands alone, 88.1% with rocks and dorks. Sarkhan's Triumph asks {2}{R}: 71.8% and 82.2% (◆ mana-analysis). Both are instant speed, so both are cast on somebody else's turn — the one-mana tutor on a turn you are already doing something, the three-mana one on the end step before the turn you intend to spend.

What is proven, and what is only declared. Four checker-passed stacks describe boards this list can still make: 001, 002, 005 and 007. Stacks 003, 004 and 006 name Aggravated Assault, Savage Ventmaw, Blasphemous Act and Wrathful Red Dragon, none of which is in the 99, and all three are marked not presentable — the verdicts stand, the boards cannot be built. deck-facts finds one combo line fully contained in this deck, Dragon Tempest + Ancient Gold Dragon at bracket 3, and zero two-card infinites. There is no infinite to fetch. The deck declares two kills and its own targets file labels both UNVERIFIED in their titles: the entry kill assembles by turn six in 10.9% of games and 21.2% with tutors modelled, the combat kill in 15.6% and 29.3% (◆ goldfish). Point a wish at either. Do not tell yourself you are fetching a combo.

Last, the funding rule. Five sources in the 99 make restricted mana (◆ deck-facts): Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon and Unclaimed Territory. Read every one and not a single coloured pip on either tutor is payable from them. Cavern of Souls and Unclaimed Territory make creature-spell-of-the-chosen-type mana; Desolation of Smaug makes Dragon-spells-only mana; Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon makes Dragon-or-Omen mana; the Halfling's any-colour mode is legendary-spells-only. Four of them — Cavern, Unclaimed Territory, Maelstrom and the Halfling — also carry a plain '{T}: Add {C}', and that colourless mana pays the {2} of Sarkhan's Triumph, the whole of Steel Hellkite, and nothing else on this sheet. It does not pay Sneak Attack's {R} either: colourless cannot pay a coloured cost, and the restricted modes are for spells while the activation is an ability. Count unrestricted red and white before you plan the turn.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three, at the end of the turn before yours. Two or three lands down, and nothing in your hand costs less than four.
targets.why: Buy the discount before you buy anything else. You draw one of the four cost reducers by turn six in 42.1% of games, mean turn 3.26 when you get one (◆ goldfish) — so in more than half of your games you do not have one, and this is the wish that fixes the hand you were actually dealt. Incubator takes {2} off every Dragon creature spell and stacks with eminence's {1}, so your six-drops cost three and The Ur-Dragon drops from nine to seven — eminence reads 'other Dragon spells' and does not cut his own cost, Incubator does. Take Herald's Horn instead when your hand is empty rather than heavy: {1} less, and its upkeep look feeds you Dragons you have not drawn. With Worldly Tutor gone these two artifacts are the only reducers any tutor in the deck reaches. ★

targets.scenario: Mid-game, four or five lands on the battlefield and the wrong ones. The commander is castable on mana count and not on colours, or Miirym is stuck behind two of her three.
targets.why: Fetch the fixing, not the payoff. This is the wish the pilot's own log says he got wrong: game 005 records 'Enlightened Tutor went for Sol Ring. It should have gone for a green rock or a signet. I had the fixing problem in front of me and tutored for speed instead.' The commander alone asks for all five colours at {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, and black is the thinnest at 52.4% on curve from lands alone and 72.9% once rocks and dorks are counted, against 71.8% red, 78.7% blue, 81.0% white and 83.1% green (◆ mana-analysis). Only two cards in the 99 carry a black pip — The Ur-Dragon and Crux of Fate — so this is a commander problem rather than a spell problem. Twelve of the 35 land copies enter tapped. Lantern gives every land you already control '{T}: Add one mana of any color', so it repairs the board in front of you rather than the board you might draw. Arcane Signet is the cheaper version of the same wish when you need one specific colour a turn sooner. ★

targets.scenario: Your turn is next and you intend to commit the commander or Miirym on it. One seat has three or more untapped lands and has answered a creature already tonight.
targets.why: Buy the answer one turn before you need it, because this tutor cannot buy it in response. The Coat has flash, but Enlightened Tutor puts it on TOP — cast the tutor at their end step, draw the Coat on your own draw step, then hold {3} through your big turn and flash it in when the removal is announced. Its entry attaches it to target legendary creature you control: 12 legendary creatures in the deck counting the commander, 11 in the library, so it needs a legendary body already down or the trigger has no legal target and you are paying equip {3}. Indestructible is not hexproof. Swords to Plowshares-class exile, bounce and -X/-X all go through it, and so does an edict. This is the V6 answer to what the log records three times — game 002 'repeated creature wipes', game 003 'targeted removal and board wipes take the deck apart now', game 005 'the refactor yanked all the counterspells and I now have zero responses'. Stated assumption: this wish is sized for a table that has shown targeted removal. Against a seat holding a sweeper, Asceticism off the same {W} is the wider card and the slower one at {3}{G}{G}. The protection figure you have is a floor — goldfish reads protection held by turn six at 55.7%, and that group names six cards the targets file has not re-derived since V6, so Asceticism, Mithril Coat and Stubborn Denial are not in it (◆ goldfish). ★

citations.quote: constant protection (boots-style equipment and enchantments — always on, cheap to re-arm, useless against wraths), single-use instants (cost held mana all game but protect at the decisive moment and can cover the board)
assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm has survived a rotation, Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest are down, and you still hold a nontoken Dragon.
targets.why: Two stacks bracket this one, and together they say the doubler is the kill rather than the margin. Stack 002 resolved that exact board with Panharmonicon: one Lathliss cast made two nonlegendary copies and 64 damage in 12 separately targeted instances, killing a 32-life opponent outright (✓ rules-verified). Stack 007 resolved the same cast with Panharmonicon removed and nothing else changed: one copy, 20 damage in 4 instances, and the 32-life seat survives at 12 — a 68.75% loss, because the doubler was doubling Terror and both Dragon Tempest abilities on every entry as well as Miirym (✓ rules-verified). Cast the artifact on a quiet turn and hold the Dragon for the loud one. Two things to know before you count on a bigger number: the copies are tokens and the 'nontoken' clause on Miirym and on Lathliss skips them, which is what keeps the cascade finite; and every one of 002's twelve instances reads 'any target', so aimed at a single seat the running total passes 40 by the eighth and a 40-life player is killable from that board (✓ stack 007 settles this point).

tutors.notes: One white mana at instant speed, and the card goes on TOP — cast it at the end of the turn before yours so your own draw step collects it. The search is revealed, so treat casting it as an announcement. Reveal Sneak Attack two turns before you use it and you have told the table which permanent to kill; game 003 is the record of what that costs, a loss the pilot read as 'I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could actually present lethal'. The 18 targets split four ways: the two reducers (Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn), the fixing (Chromatic Lantern, Arcane Signet, Dragon's Hoard, Talisman of Dominance), the protection (Mithril Coat, Lightning Greaves, Asceticism) and the payoffs (Panharmonicon, Dragon Tempest, Temur Ascendancy, Garruk's Uprising, Sneak Attack, Steel Hellkite, the two Dragonstorms, Sol Ring). Sneak Attack is the one whose ceiling is already proven: stack 005 priced {R} putting Drakuseth, Maw of Flames onto the battlefield with haste at 17 damage, all of it standing after the mandatory end-step sacrifice, and settled that it cannot touch the commander in the command zone (✓ rules-verified). ★

targets.scenario: Turn six or later, at an opponent's end step. You will have five mana next turn, the commander is still in the command zone, and the table has stopped watching your combat step.
targets.why: Rent the commander instead of buying him. The Ur-Dragon has a mean cast turn of 6.881 and a median of 7; he arrives by turn six in 33.3% of games, and in 2,277 of 10,000 he never arrives by turn ten at all (◆ goldfish). Courser costs {4}{R}{R}, five with eminence, and his entry puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield with haste — so you attack, draw a card for each attacking Dragon, and put a permanent from hand onto the battlefield, and he returns to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step with no tax accrued, because the tax counts casts and this was a put. Fetch at their end step, cast on yours, attack the same turn. Two costs: the Courser is a 6/5 that has to survive resolution to do any of it, and returning the commander at end step means the removal you did not hold up hits the Courser instead.

citations.quote: A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.

targets.scenario: Turn four or five, two or three Dragons still in hand, and the last two games at this table were lost by committing the board a turn early.
targets.why: Fetch the timing, not the body. Whirlwing Stormbrood costs {4}{U}, four with eminence, has flash itself, and reads 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash' — so every Dragon after it lands at the end of the turn before yours and swings before the table has a turn to answer it. That is the effect of haste without the board being read a rotation early, which is the loss the log files three times: 'I pour it into the board too early and telegraph' (game 005), 'the table read Sean is swinging for 28 in the air and they converged immediately' (game 003). The price is a blue pip at 78.7% on curve from lands alone and 88.1% with rocks and dorks (◆ mana-analysis), and a 4/3 body that blocks nothing relevant. Take Transcendent Dragon instead when the thing you need is the answer rather than the timing: {4}{U}{U}, five with eminence, flash, and its entry counters target spell if you cast it, exiles that spell and lets you cast it for free. Both want mana held, and you have leftover mana to hold on 51.0% of turn sixes (◆ goldfish, interaction castable — a floor, since the model spends everything it can every turn). No goldfish figure prices flash or the counter; the model reads only the body.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: Dragon Tempest is on the battlefield, you can reach six mana next turn including {W}{W}, and one opponent has no flying blocker.
targets.why: This is the deck's loudest contained line and it has a stack behind it. Ancient Gold Dragon costs {5}{W}{W}, six with eminence; connect once and the d20 makes that many 1/1 flying Faerie Dragons at the same time. Stack 001 fixed the roll at 15 and resolved the cascade: Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times, each trigger dealt X = 17 on that board of two other Dragons, and the 30-life opponent died to the second trigger aimed at them (✓ rules-verified). Two findings from that stack to plan around. Miirym does not copy the tokens, because they are tokens. And every trigger locks its target when it goes on the stack, so triggers aimed at a player who has already left the game fizzle — spread them rather than stacking them on one seat. Two costs before you fetch: {W}{W} on a deck at 81.0% white on curve from lands alone (◆ mana-analysis), and no goldfish figure prices this card at all, since meta.combat_effects_not_modelled names Ancient Gold Dragon as an effect the model cannot read.

targets.scenario: Five or six mana, most of it from Cavern of Souls, Unclaimed Territory, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon or a Treasure, and the colours in front of you do not cast the Dragons in your hand.
targets.why: The Dragon your restricted mana can actually pay for. Steel Hellkite is {6} with no coloured pip — enumerated from the 23 Dragon creature cards in the library, it is the only one with none — so the plain '{T}: Add {C}' on Cavern of Souls, Unclaimed Territory, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon and Delighted Halfling pays for all of it, and with Dragon chosen their any-colour modes pay too, since it is a creature spell of the chosen type. It is also removal on a body, which is the axis the pilot says he is missing: {X} destroys each nonland permanent with mana value X whose controller was dealt combat damage by it this turn, once each turn — X = 0 sweeps that one seat's tokens and Treasures, X = 3 takes the rock or the enchantment that is holding you up. It costs a 5/5 flier's worth of damage and one attack to set up, and it reaches only the seat you hit. One more reason to know this card: it is the single card both tutors in the deck can find, and the only Enlightened Tutor target Herald's Horn can pull off the top.

tutors.notes: The only tutor here that puts the card in your HAND — no transit turn, no draw step spent — so this is the one you cast on the turn you need the card, and the one to keep for the piece you cannot afford to telegraph a turn early. It pays for that with reach: 23 Dragon creature cards and nothing else. No Sneak Attack, no Panharmonicon, no land, no protection spell, and none of the four cost reducers — Urza's Incubator and Herald's Horn are artifacts, Dragonspeaker Shaman is a Human Barbarian Shaman and Dragonlord's Servant a Goblin Shaman. Whirlwing Stormbrood counts, because its front face is a Dragon creature. Three mana at instant speed on the colour that runs 71.8% on curve from lands alone and 82.2% with rocks and dorks (◆ mana-analysis) still means you shop on somebody else's end step and keep your whole turn to cast what you found. When the board already has a payoff down and needs a multiplier instead, Thrakkus the Butcher at {3}{R}{G} is the half of THE COMBAT KILL you can fetch and cast off seven mana — that kill assembles by turn six in 15.6% of games and 29.3% with tutors modelled, no stack has resolved it, and the targets file labels it UNVERIFIED in its own title (◆ goldfish).

gaps: Worldly Tutor is out and nothing replaced its reach. It was the only search that found a creature, which means the deck now has no route to Dragonspeaker Shaman, Dragonlord's Servant or any of its five mana dorks except drawing them. Two of the four cost reducers and all of the colour fixing that walks are outside both remaining searches. The reducer-by-turn-six figures above (42.1% unassisted, 55.8% assisted) are the measure of what that costs, and they were run on this list.

goldfish_targets.json has not been re-derived since v1.3.0 and three of its groups name cards that are no longer in the 99. THE ENTRY KILL lists Sarkhan, Fireblood and Utvara Hellkite; the Dragon-restricted-mana group lists Sarkhan, Fireblood, leaving only Desolation of Smaug. The RATES are still correct for the cards that remain — an any_of group cannot draw a card the deck does not contain — but the LABELS name a bigger group than the deck has, and a reader will size the plan off the label. Separately, 'Protection held for the big turn' names six cards and V6 added three more protection effects (Asceticism, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial), so 55.7% by turn six is a floor for the current list rather than its rate. Hand this to a goldfish-targets re-derivation, not to prose.

engine.json is stale against this decklist and is therefore not used as a source of composition anywhere above. Twelve cards it assigns to stages are not in the 99 — Worldly Tutor, Utvara Hellkite, Sarkhan Fireblood, Radiant Destiny, Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise, Fabled Passage, Forbidden Orchard, Prismatic Vista, Shivan Reef, Stormcarved Coast and Tarnished Citadel — and none of the seven V6 arrivals is assigned to a stage at all. Its stage labels are still the deck's vocabulary; its card lists need a re-run of analyze-engine.

There is no verified win line, and two of the wishes above point at kills the deck only declares. THE ENTRY KILL assembles by turn six in 10.9% of games and THE COMBAT KILL in 15.6% (21.2% and 29.3% with tutors modelled, ◆ goldfish), and both carry UNVERIFIED in their own titles because no stack has resolved either. The line the V6 notes call key is also unproven as a line: Hellkite Courser putting The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield, attacking, drawing off the attack trigger and putting a permanent down, then returning him at end step. A resolve-stack run on that board would settle the deck's most-fetched wish and is the single highest-value stack this guide can name.

No wish reaches the graveyard, and this is absolute: a search of every oracle text in the 99 for 'from your graveyard' returns zero cards. The only card that mentions a graveyard at all is Transcendent Dragon, and it mentions it to exile a countered spell instead. Nothing here rebuys a Dragon that has died. Play around removal rather than planning to answer it after the fact — which is what the V6 protection package is for, and why three of its six spells are held rather than cast.

Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon is a third search this guide does not cover: {4}, {T}, sacrifice it, search for a Dragon card and put it into your hand. It is a land, so it belongs to the mana analysis rather than to this sheet, and its clause is wider on paper than Sarkhan's Triumph's — 'a Dragon card' rather than 'a Dragon creature card' — but in this 99 every Dragon card is a creature, so the two reach the same 23. Price it before you rely on it: four mana plus the land itself, and unlike a fetchland it puts nothing back.

The V6 protection package is unmeasured at a table, and the instruments say why. The goldfish has no opponents and cannot read flash, a counter or indestructible — it read only the bodies of Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood and Steel Hellkite. Forge on the pre-V6 list never cast Teferi's Protection or Deflecting Swat in 40 games, so a Forge rate on a held protection card is a floor at best; Lightning Greaves was cast 5 and equipped 5, which is why Mithril Coat, an equipment that attaches itself, is at least visible to that harness. Treat every claim above about holding up mana as a stated assumption about this pilot's table, not as a measured rate.
